standards.title: ZLIB Compressed Data Format Specification version 3.3

normative_inventory.scope: Atomic case-insensitive normative must, should, and recommended clauses in pre-BCP 14 prose; may, optional, and need-not permissions are excluded.

requirements.summary: The bounded zlib decoder accepts and decompresses conforming byte-aligned zlib streams within the caller's explicit resource contract.
The Deflate content encoder produces a complete conforming zlib wrapper rather than a raw DEFLATE stream.
Encoded CMF and FLG bytes satisfy the RFC modulo-31 FCHECK invariant.
The compressor emits the required CMF and FLG header and the correct terminal ADLER32 checksum.
HTTP Deflate encoding rejects caller dictionary state and therefore never sets FDICT for this embedding format.
The decoder validates CMF, FLG, and ADLER32 independently and reports malformed input on any incorrect value.
A syntactically checkable header using an unsupported compression method is rejected as invalid encoding.
An FDICT stream whose DICTID has no authorized preset dictionary is rejected with a typed dictionary error.
A zlib embedding format must support every preset dictionary that the embedding format specifies.
requirements.reason: The HTTP Deflate content coding implemented here specifies no zlib preset dictionaries; dictionary transport uses separately typed Brotli and Zstandard codings and never reaches the zlib wrapper.

requirements.summary: Because HTTP Deflate defines no preset dictionary, every received zlib stream carrying FDICT is rejected.
A compressor and decompressor using the optional zlib dictionary feature must use exactly the same dictionary.
requirements.reason: The public HTTP Deflate coding rejects dictionaries on both encode and decode, so no zlib preset-dictionary session can be established or mismatched.

requirements.summary: A standard data format using zlib preset dictionaries must define its allowed dictionaries precisely.
requirements.reason: This package implements existing HTTP content codings and does not define a standard data format that embeds zlib with the optional preset-dictionary feature.

requirements.summary: The ADLER32 calculation begins with the required recommended initial checksum value of one.

standards.title: DEFLATE Compressed Data Format Specification version 1.3

normative_inventory.scope: Atomic case-insensitive normative must, should, and recommended clauses in pre-BCP 14 prose; may, optional, and need-not permissions are excluded.

requirements.summary: The bounded DEFLATE decoder accepts conforming stored, fixed-Huffman, dynamic-Huffman, and maximum-range streams.
The Deflate content encoder emits complete conforming DEFLATE data inside the required zlib wrapper.
DEFLATE block fields and Huffman codes use the RFC's defined bit-to-byte packing order without host-endian dependence.
The compressor does not emit Huffman codes beyond the format maxima and the decoder rejects malformed dynamic trees.
Symbols with zero bit length receive no Huffman value in emitted trees and malformed tree assignments are rejected.
Length and distance extra-bit integers are interpreted least-significant bit first as corrected by reported erratum 7764.
Zero-length literal, length, and distance symbols do not participate in Huffman tree construction.
The decoder accepts the maximum 258-byte match and 32768-byte backward distance defined by DEFLATE.
The streaming decoder accepts large and multi-block representations subject only to the caller's explicit finite resource limits.
A compressor implementor is strongly recommended to follow the historical algorithm described to avoid then-relevant patent coverage.
requirements.reason: The repository does not implement or redistribute a DEFLATE compression algorithm; it uses the explicitly permitted OTP runtime zlib service, and this historical patent rationale is not wire behavior.

requirements.summary: Systems using DEFLATE provide an integrity check for compressed data instead of silently accepting corruption.

entries.reason: The published MSB-first sentence conflicts with the section 3.1 packing rule and interoperable DEFLATE wire behavior; the proposed LSB-first correction is applied.
The proposed insertion of the word length disambiguates the prose but does not alter the defined Huffman construction or interoperable decoder behavior.

normative_inventory.scope: Atomic case-insensitive normative must, should, and recommended clauses in pre-BCP 14 prose; may, optional, and need-not permissions are excluded.

requirements.summary: The bounded gzip decoder accepts conforming minimal, optional-header, and concatenated-member representations.
The gzip encoder emits a deterministic complete member with a conforming header, DEFLATE payload, and trailer.
An emitted optional original filename must consist only of ISO 8859-1 characters.
requirements.reason: The public HTTP gzip encoder accepts content bytes only and always emits the minimal deterministic header with FNAME clear, so it cannot emit filename metadata in any character set.

requirements.summary: A filename from an operating system using another character set must be translated into ISO 8859-1.
requirements.reason: No filesystem filename or filename encoding enters the content-coding API and the encoder always leaves FNAME clear; operating-system name translation is therefore unreachable.

requirements.summary: An emitted optional gzip comment must consist only of ISO 8859-1 characters.
requirements.reason: The encoder exposes no comment metadata and emits the deterministic minimal gzip header with FCOMMENT clear, so it cannot serialize a nonconforming comment.

requirements.summary: Line breaks in an emitted optional gzip comment should use one line-feed byte.
requirements.reason: The public encoder never emits FCOMMENT and accepts no comment text, leaving no line-ending metadata to normalize.

requirements.summary: The three reserved bits in every emitted gzip FLG byte are zero.
The compressor emits correct ID1, ID2, compression method, CRC32, and uncompressed input size fields.
The compliant gzip compressor sets every reserved header flag bit to zero.
The decoder validates both gzip identification bytes and compression method and rejects every incorrect value.
The decoder parses or skips bounded FEXTRA, XLEN, FNAME, FCOMMENT, and FHCRC fields before the compressed payload.
A gzip member with any nonzero reserved FLG bit is rejected rather than misparsed as a known header layout.
The gzip decoder validates the CRC32 integrity field and fails closed on compressed-data corruption.

entries.reason: The verified correction changes the displayed Apollo subfield identifier from uppercase P to the lowercase p represented by byte 0x70; unknown subfields are skipped identically.

normative_inventory.scope: Atomic uppercase BCP 14 mandatory and advisory clauses; MAY and OPTIONAL are excluded.

entries.reason: The verified correction updates obsolete scheme-design guidance from RFC 2718 to RFC 4395 and changes no URI grammar or runtime behavior.
The verified correction removes an accidental hyperlink from an algorithm example and has no source-text or resolution behavior effect.
The unverified proposal would add backslash to unreserved characters despite the published ABNF and established URI processing; the strict redirect boundary retains the published grammar.
The held proposal adds host-language slash delimiters and escapes to an illustrative regular expression; the product does not use that non-validating appendix expression.
The held clarification of abnormal excess-parent examples is not a verified grammar change; executable resolution vectors retain the published remove-dot-segments behavior.
The held alternative merge rule for a base ending in slash-dot-dot has not updated STD 66, so the standards-library merge algorithm remains authoritative.
The held host-prose proposal does not alter the published reg-name ABNF; HTTP redirect admission separately requires a nonempty validated authority.
The held proposal adds a redundant path-abempty alternative to relative-part; slash references already resolve through the published path-absolute alternative.
Replacing the zero-repetition spelling of path-empty with an empty quoted string only clarifies equivalent ABNF and changes no accepted URI.
The held pseudocode wording would pass the base object rather than naming only its path; the following merge procedure already uses the base authority and behavior is unchanged.
The rejected proposal would add hash to fragment content and therefore does not modify the published URI-reference grammar.
The rejected proposal incorrectly makes scheme mandatory in a URI-reference, whose relative-ref production deliberately permits no scheme.
The rejected dec-octet alternative reordering addresses parser strategy rather than ABNF validity and does not change IPv4 syntax.
The rejected expanded IPv6 grammar is not a correction to the equivalent published alternatives and cannot change accepted address literals.
The rejected proposal inserts a hash into the scheme capture of the illustrative regular expression contrary to the deliberate URI-reference syntax.
The rejected report supplied no actionable corrected text for the explicitly non-validating appendix parser and changes no normative grammar.
The rejected URL-only wording was superseded by verified erratum 2525's updated URI-scheme reference and has no runtime effect.
The rejected proposal confuses the four hier-part path forms with the five general path forms and does not alter the published ABNF.

requirements.summary: Base64 serialization never inserts line feeds or other folding characters into encoded output.
Structured Field Byte Sequence serialization includes the exact required terminal Base64 padding.
Base64 input containing whitespace, URL-safe substitutions, or any character outside the selected alphabet is rejected.
Encoders emit zero unused pad bits and decoders reject noncanonical encodings whose discarded pad bits are nonzero.

entries.reason: The verified correction fixes an off-by-one archival reference URL and does not change any Base-N alphabet or encoding behavior.
The verified note clarifies that displayed test strings denote input octets; executable vectors use explicit byte arrays and are unaffected.
The verified subject-verb correction changes prose only and leaves the zero-pad-bit requirement unchanged.
The verified change replaces the indefinite article before URI and has no URL-safe alphabet or padding effect.
The unverified proposal clarifies Base32 final input grouping; this product publishes only the standard Base64 form required by Structured Fields.
The reported addition states the bit order already implied by the published octet and six-bit-group algorithm, so interoperable Base64 wire bytes do not change.

normative_inventory.scope: Atomic uppercase BCP 14 mandatory and advisory clauses; MAY and OPTIONAL are excluded.

requirements.summary: Every emitted ALPN extension_data value contains one length-delimited ProtocolNameList.
Configuration, encoding, and decoding all reject an empty ProtocolName.
Protocol names over 255 bytes and truncated length-delimited input fail closed rather than being shortened.
The server emits exactly one selected ProtocolName and the client rejects zero or multiple server selections.
Selection walks the configured server preference list and chooses its first value also advertised by the client.
No protocol overlap produces fatal no_application_protocol and a wire-visible QUIC CRYPTO_ERROR value 0x178.
The authenticated selected protocol is immutable connection state and is the value exposed for the connection lifetime.
A connected server retains one immutable selected ALPN and has no API or state transition that can replace it for later application data.
A newly registered identifier that leaks sensitive information should not be configured where visible in cleartext.
requirements.reason: The project does not define or register a new ALPN identifier. Its generic configuration documentation nevertheless warns callers that identifiers are externally observable and must not encode account, tenant, user, or other identifying data.

requirements.summary: A specification for a sensitive new ALPN identifier should recommend against cleartext-visible deployment.
requirements.reason: This repository consumes registered ALPN identifiers but does not publish a specification or registry entry for a new identifier; the public client and server configuration docs still give the corresponding non-sensitive-identifier warning.

entries.reason: The rejected report proposed registering historical HTTP/0.9 and HTTP/1.0 identifiers through errata; it does not change the ALPN extension format or negotiation behavior.

requirements.summary: Every emitted JSON text sequence uses UTF-8 encoding.
The qlog writer never emits UTF-16 or UTF-32 JSON sequence records.
The qualification parser treats each RS-delimited octet string as UTF-8 JSON.
A general JSON sequence parser should continue after an invalid record.
requirements.reason: This project exposes only an encoder. Its qualification-only parser deliberately fails closed because any malformed project-generated qlog is evidence corruption, not untrusted application input.

requirements.summary: Each encoded record is exactly an RS prefix, one complete JSON text, and an LF suffix.
An encoder accepting pre-encoded JSON should validate it before framing.
requirements.reason: The qlog API accepts typed numeric events only and constructs every JSON record internally; it has no raw or pre-encoded JSON input path.

requirements.summary: A sequence parser should offer a warning for truncated JSON text records.
requirements.reason: The internal qualification parser has no warning mode because a truncated generated trace is always a fatal gate error reported with a typed reason and nonzero exit status.

requirements.summary: The qualification parser cannot accept a possibly truncated top-level scalar without trailing JSON whitespace.
Potentially truncated non-self-delimited top-level values are rejected rather than returned.
An encoder not producing its own JSON should ensure that supplied texts are complete.
requirements.reason: All qlog JSON is constructed from bounded typed arguments inside the writer, so no externally encoded or potentially incomplete JSON text can be supplied.

requirements.summary: Malformed qualification input produces a controlled diagnostic failure instead of an uncontrolled parser crash.

entries.reason: The apostrophe correction changes prose only and has no framing or implementation effect.
Removing the duplicated words changes prose only and has no parser behavior effect.

standards.title: Happy Eyeballs Version 2: Better Connectivity Using Concurrency

requirements.summary: An ORIGIN frame is sent only on HTTP/2 stream zero.
A client ignores an ORIGIN frame received on a nonzero stream.
A client ignores ORIGIN on an h2c connection.
requirements.reason: The product has no h2c client path; its HTTP/2 client requires authenticated HTTPS with the h2 ALPN, while cleartext prior knowledge is server-only and a server never consumes peer ORIGIN authority.

requirements.summary: A client ignores ORIGIN when an unknown incompatible low flag is set.
An HTTP intermediary does not forward hop-by-hop ORIGIN frames.
requirements.reason: The product does not implement an HTTP/2 forward-intermediary role; its explicit CONNECT client establishes an opaque tunnel and cannot forward decoded HTTP/2 control frames.

requirements.summary: A proxy-configured client ignores ORIGIN received from the proxy itself.
requirements.reason: The only proxy mode is HTTP CONNECT followed by end-to-end authenticated TLS; after tunnel establishment HTTP/2 frames come from the origin endpoint, not from the proxy.

requirements.summary: Every length-delimited field is parsed as an ASCII origin serialization.
An invalid individual ASCII-Origin field is ignored without losing valid siblings.
A 421 response removes the request origin from future use on that connection.
A pooled connection is never considered authoritative outside its accepted origin key.
A client should reuse an authoritative connection for origins advertised in its Origin Set.
requirements.reason: The finite pool deliberately reuses only the connection's original authenticated origin key; peer ORIGIN advertisements are observable but do not expand authority until cross-origin certificate revalidation is available.

requirements.summary: A client should avoid a connection whose Origin Set is a proper subset of another viable set.
requirements.reason: The pool does not rank peer-advertised Origin Sets because it intentionally partitions sessions by one exact authenticated origin; safe exact reuse is preferred over unaudited cross-origin coalescing.

requirements.summary: A client should close an idle connection whose Origin Set is a proper subset.
requirements.reason: Because peer-advertised Origin Sets never expand pool authority, the pool has no proper-subset ordering to retire; it instead applies finite idle expiry and immediately evicts a connection after status 421.

requirements.summary: SETTINGS_ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL accepts and emits only the values zero and one.
A peer that enabled Extended CONNECT cannot subsequently disable it, including within one ordered SETTINGS payload.
An Extended CONNECT request is rejected unless both :scheme and :path are present and valid.
Extended CONNECT authority is request metadata for the configured local handler and is never treated as an instruction to dial that authority.
An HTTP/2 WebSocket handshake requires Extended CONNECT protocol metadata rather than an HTTP/1 Upgrade request.
The typed WebSocket handshake accepts only the registered websocket Extended CONNECT protocol token.
HTTP/2 WebSocket handshakes admit the HTTP target scheme for ws and HTTPS for wss while rejecting every other scheme.
Connection and Upgrade fields are neither generated nor accepted on an HTTP/2 WebSocket Extended CONNECT handshake.

requirements.summary: A receiver accepts every value of the seven unused Version Negotiation first-byte bits and assigns them no semantics.
A Version Negotiation packet with no Supported Version field or a truncated final field is rejected before it can change endpoint state.
The listener copies the received Source Connection ID into the Version Negotiation Destination Connection ID.
The listener copies the received Destination Connection ID into the Version Negotiation Source Connection ID.
A client can tentatively change only to an originally offered compatible version and accepts that choice only after authenticated transport parameters prove the server's version set.

standards.title: QUIC: A UDP-Based Multiplexed and Secure Transport
QUIC Loss Detection and Congestion Control

normative_inventory.scope: Atomic uppercase BCP 14 mandatory and advisory clauses; MAY and OPTIONAL are excluded.

requirements.summary: An ACK that does not newly acknowledge its largest packet does not update the RTT estimator.
An ACK creates no RTT sample unless it newly acknowledges at least one ack-eliciting packet.
The first real RTT sample initializes min_rtt to exactly the latest observed RTT.
Every later sample retains the lesser of the existing min_rtt and latest_rtt.
Persistent congestion refreshes min_rtt from the newest authenticated RTT sample.
The implementation refreshes min_rtt only on the explicit persistent-congestion transition.
Before handshake confirmation, RTT adjustment does not cap ACK delay at max_ack_delay.
The normative adjustment procedure ignores the peer maximum ACK delay until confirmation.
After confirmation, RTT adjustment uses the lesser of reported and maximum ACK delay.
ACK delay is never subtracted when doing so would make the adjusted sample smaller than min_rtt.
Locally postponed pre-confirmation ACK processing should subtract its local key-wait delay.
requirements.reason: This stack never queues an encrypted ACK for processing before its packet-protection keys exist; only successfully decrypted packets reach recovery, so no local key-wait interval exists to subtract.

requirements.summary: Packet-threshold loss detection starts at the recommended distance of three packets.
The fixed packet reordering threshold cannot be configured below three packets.
An earlier in-flight packet is declared lost after a later same-space packet is acknowledged and the time threshold passes.
The time loss threshold is always at least the local timer granularity.
A not-yet-lost packet before the largest ACK schedules its remaining time-threshold deadline.
Time-threshold loss detection uses the recommended nine-eighths RTT multiplier.
The live recovery owner uses the recommended one millisecond timer granularity.
PTO expiry increments backoff and requests probes without declaring any outstanding packet lost.
The four-times RTT variation component floors every PTO base at timer granularity.
The connection deadline selects the earlier Initial or Handshake recovery timer.
Application Data recovery cannot arm a PTO before handshake confirmation.
Sending, newly acknowledging, or discarding keys recomputes recovery from current packet state and RTT.
Every PTO expiration increments one bounded exponent shared across packet number spaces.
A present time-threshold loss deadline suppresses the packet space PTO deadline.
A path without historical RTT starts from the recommended 333 millisecond estimate.
A PATH_CHALLENGE round trip should not become a normal RTT estimator sample.
requirements.reason: The implementation does not exercise the optional preceding behavior of deriving a new-path initial RTT from PATH_CHALLENGE delay; path validation time never enters the RTT estimator.

requirements.summary: Discarding Initial or Handshake keys removes that space's loss and PTO timer state.

An amplification-blocked server arms no PTO it lacks budget to transmit, and a prepared probe which exhausts the remaining credit is retained as pending work rather than converted into a fatal connection error.
An unconfirmed client without a Handshake ACK arms an anti-deadlock PTO even with no packet in flight.
The anti-deadlock PTO selects a Handshake probe whenever Handshake write keys exist.
Without Handshake keys, anti-deadlock recovery selects Initial and the wire sender pads its datagram to 1200 bytes.

Every fired PTO makes at least one ack-eliciting probe ready in the expired packet space: already queued delivery work is preferred, otherwise ownership of the oldest reliable outstanding frame is transferred, and only an empty space falls back to PING.
The bounded PTO allowance can only be consumed by ack-eliciting in-flight packets; automatic probe work is either reliable delivery state transferred exactly once or a PING fallback.
A PTO should also coalesce an ack-eliciting probe from another packet space that has in-flight data.
Queued control, CRYPTO, or stream delivery work is used as the probe before recovery retransmission or a PING fallback, without dropping later data that can share the packet.
When no application or retransmission data exists, PTO sends a PING to rearm recovery.
Discarding packet-protection keys clears every sent-packet recovery record for that space.
The same key-discard transition removes all affected in-flight bytes from congestion accounting.
Selecting CUBIC preserves bounded flight, pacing, loss response, ECN response, and application-limited safeguards.
Normal in-flight sends are refused when their bytes would exceed cwnd; only an active PTO allowance bypasses the gate.
NewReno starts at min(10 times max_datagram_size, max(14720, twice max_datagram_size)).
A maximum datagram size change should recalculate an otherwise unchanged initial congestion window.
requirements.reason: A validated path-size change immediately updates the controller's datagram unit and minimum-window floor, but deliberately preserves the accumulated congestion window instead of guessing whether it still represents the initial flight.

requirements.summary: A handshake-only datagram-size reduction should reset cwnd to the new initial value.
requirements.reason: The path-size adapter has no trustworthy signal that a decrease occurred specifically to complete the handshake, so it preserves current cwnd while updating the datagram unit and reduction floor.

requirements.summary: NewReno loss and persistent-congestion reductions floor cwnd at two maximum datagrams.
A first packet loss or ECN-CE increase exits NewReno slow start into recovery.
Entering a NewReno recovery period sets ssthresh to half cwnd, bounded by the minimum window.
The congestion window is reduced immediately on recovery entry and remains reduced when recovery exits.
Congestion avoidance adds at most one maximum datagram after one whole congestion window is acknowledged.
Loss classification retains every packet sent after the earliest acknowledged packet in its number space.
A granted PTO probe bypasses a full congestion window without opening the gate for ordinary sends.
PTO probe bytes enter congestion and a bounded recovery ledger even when they exceed cwnd.
Persistent-congestion duration multiplies the current PTO base by the recommended threshold of three.
Both boundary packets used to establish a persistent-congestion interval are ack-eliciting.
Persistent congestion cannot start unless a real RTT sample existed when both boundary packets were sent.
Persistent-congestion interval construction should compare send times across all packet number spaces.
requirements.reason: The bounded recovery ledger intentionally uses the RFC-permitted fallback of the packet space that was acknowledged; it retains ACK barriers in that space but does not hold a second cross-space send-time index.

requirements.summary: A live persistent-congestion event collapses cwnd to the controller's minimum window.

Every in-flight live send reserves finite pacing credit derived from current cwnd and smoothed RTT. Pending work arms its exact release, including an immediate wake when it is already pacing-ready, while a full congestion window suppresses that zero-delay retry.
A bounded token-bucket pacer limits every in-flight burst and returns an exact release deadline.
The default pacer burst is bounded to ten current path-sized datagrams, matching the initial window.
Packets containing only ACK frames bypass pacing because they are not classified in flight.
Neither slow start nor congestion avoidance grows cwnd when the pre-ACK flight did not fill it.
An ACK batch snapshots full utilization before removing packets, so pacing delay alone cannot suppress legitimate growth.

entries.reason: The verified correction computes the rttvar sample against the old smoothed_rtt before updating smoothed_rtt; update_existing preserves that ordering.

normative_inventory.scope: Atomic uppercase BCP 14 mandatory and advisory clauses; MAY and OPTIONAL are excluded.

requirements.summary: The encoder emits field representations in the input field-section order.
The encoder does not insert or duplicate when that growth would evict an unacknowledged referenced entry.
The encoder never risks more streams than the peer SETTINGS_QPACK_BLOCKED_STREAMS value.
A decoder rejects blocked-stream use above its advertised bound as QPACK_DECOMPRESSION_FAILED.
QPACK instructions are submitted as one bounded resource write and retained when full credit is unavailable.
The decoder returns field lines in representation order.
Blocked field-section data should remain charged to receive flow control until decoder state arrives.
requirements.reason: The public QUIC stream adapter delivers already-accounted bounded chunks before QPACK can inspect Required Insert Count. HTTP/3 therefore retains those bytes in a per-stream and aggregate connection budget instead of pretending credit was not consumed; exceeding either ceiling fails closed.

requirements.summary: A Required Insert Count smaller than the referenced dynamic state causes QPACK_DECOMPRESSION_FAILED.
Completing a field section with dynamic references queues a Section Acknowledgment.
Evicted or out-of-range dynamic references in field sections cause QPACK_DECOMPRESSION_FAILED.
Evicted or missing dynamic references on the encoder stream cause QPACK_ENCODER_STREAM_ERROR.
An invalid static-table index in a field representation causes QPACK_DECOMPRESSION_FAILED.
An invalid static-table index on the encoder stream causes QPACK_ENCODER_STREAM_ERROR.
Duplicate name-value entries remain valid dynamic-table insertions.
Capacity changes and insertions cannot evict a referenced dynamic entry.
An encoder-stream insertion larger than active capacity is rejected as QPACK_ENCODER_STREAM_ERROR.
The encoder cannot set dynamic capacity above the decoder-advertised maximum.
A server accepting HTTP/3 0-RTT with remembered non-zero capacity repeats that setting.
requirements.reason: The current API can resume QUIC with 0-RTT keys but never exposes or sends HTTP/3 field sections before authenticated peer SETTINGS are received. Therefore no QPACK encoder state or remembered QPACK setting is used in early data.

requirements.summary: A zero maximum dynamic-table capacity prevents every insertion.
A zero maximum capacity produces no encoder-stream instructions.
The prefixed-integer codec accepts the complete unsigned 62-bit QUIC integer range.
Each endpoint creates at most one QPACK encoder stream and one QPACK decoder stream.
A second peer encoder or decoder stream causes H3_STREAM_CREATION_ERROR.
The endpoint never sends FIN on its QPACK encoder or decoder critical stream.
The endpoint does not issue STOP_SENDING for a peer QPACK critical stream.
FIN or reset on a QPACK critical stream causes H3_CLOSED_CRITICAL_STREAM.
Both QPACK critical stream types are accepted even when configured table capacity is zero.
A Set Dynamic Table Capacity value cannot exceed the peer's configured ceiling.
The decoder maps an excessive capacity instruction to QPACK_ENCODER_STREAM_ERROR.
Reducing capacity cannot evict any entry still held by an unacknowledged field section.
Acknowledging a stream with no outstanding dynamic section causes QPACK_DECODER_STREAM_ERROR.
A zero or excessive Insert Count Increment causes QPACK_DECODER_STREAM_ERROR.
An Encoded Insert Count impossible for a conformant encoder causes QPACK_DECOMPRESSION_FAILED.
The encoder never emits a field-section prefix whose reconstructed Base is negative.
A sign bit with Required Insert Count not above Delta Base is rejected as QPACK_DECOMPRESSION_FAILED.
A field marked never-indexed is encoded only with a literal representation.
A QPACK intermediary forwarding a received N-bit field retains a literal never-indexed representation.
requirements.reason: The library does not expose an automatic HTTP intermediary that forwards decoded QPACK fields. Client proxy configuration selects an outbound transport but never re-encodes peer response fields as a new request.

requirements.summary: An intermediary never converts a received never-indexed literal into an indexed representation.
requirements.reason: No automatic intermediary forwarding API consumes decoded QPACK never-index metadata, so the conditional re-encoding operation is unavailable rather than silently dropping the protection.

requirements.summary: QPACK re-encoding by an intermediary uses a literal with the N bit set.
requirements.reason: The product does not provide automatic intermediary re-encoding; callers can explicitly preserve the typed never-index bit, but no decoded peer field is implicitly forwarded.

requirements.summary: Translation to HPACK preserves received QPACK N-bit fields as HPACK never-indexed literals.
requirements.reason: The library intentionally has no automatic HTTP/3-to-HTTP/2 intermediary translation path, so it cannot consume and accidentally weaken received QPACK never-index metadata.

requirements.summary: Integer and string limits cover the configured maximum field-section size while remaining finite.
Values above configured decode limits map to decompression or the matching critical-stream QPACK error code.

entries.reason: The verified correction makes Required Insert Count one greater than the largest zero-based dynamic index, matching the normative algorithm.
The proposal changes CORS spellings and removes an entry, but it is held rather than verified and cannot alter the published fixed QPACK wire indices without an updating standard.

standards.title: The Proxy-Status HTTP Response Header Field

requirements.summary: Every accepted Proxy-Status list member identifies its intermediary with a Structured Fields String or Token.
The safe append operation retains the existing origin-to-client intermediary chain before adding the local member.
The role-aware field generator refuses Proxy-Status generation by an origin server.
The role-aware generator rejects trailer placement when the Proxy-Status value could still be sent in headers.
Every generated trailer member must match a character-identical intermediary member announced in the header section.
Unknown parameters do not affect registered semantics and the default public diagnostic view removes them.
A generating intermediary selects the most specific registered proxy error that accurately describes its failure.
requirements.reason: The codec has no transport or application failure context from which to infer a proxy error type; it preserves the caller-selected token exactly so policy can select a deployment-accurate registered or extension value.

requirements.summary: An intermediary-generated HTTP response normally uses the response status recommended for its selected proxy error type.
requirements.reason: This module encodes and decodes a field value but never chooses or generates an HTTP response status; that response-policy decision remains outside the value codec.

requirements.summary: The next-protocol parameter accepts only a nonempty bounded ALPN identifier represented as Token or Byte Sequence.
An ALPN identifier representable as an ASCII Structured Fields Token is rejected in Byte Sequence form.
The received-status registered parameter accepts only an integer HTTP status value.

requirements.summary: SETTINGS_NO_RFC7540_PRIORITIES accepts only the wire values zero and one.
An invalid SETTINGS_NO_RFC7540_PRIORITIES value is classified as an HTTP/2 protocol connection error.
An endpoint using SETTINGS_NO_RFC7540_PRIORITIES sends it only in its first SETTINGS frame.
A sender cannot change SETTINGS_NO_RFC7540_PRIORITIES after its first SETTINGS frame.
A server receiving SETTINGS_NO_RFC7540_PRIORITIES equal to one ignores RFC 7540 priority signals.

Same-urgency incremental responses share bandwidth using bounded round-robin scheduling.

Backend scheduling state derived from client priority remains scoped to one client connection.

requirements.summary: An endpoint sends no DATAGRAM frame until a nonzero peer max_datagram_frame_size has been authenticated, including remembered state for 0-RTT.

Receiving DATAGRAM without locally advertised support is classified as PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
Receiving a DATAGRAM frame larger than the local advertised limit is classified as PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
The default receive policy advertises 65535 so every DATAGRAM fitting a QUIC packet is admissible before tighter endpoint limits.
A server accepts early data only when the current remembered 0-RTT parameter set is compatible; the equality-only policy is stricter than the required nondecrease.
A resumed client compares the fresh max_datagram_frame_size, treating omission as zero, with its ticket-authenticated value before overwriting it.
A fresh server DATAGRAM limit below the stored 0-RTT value, including omission, produces PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
HTTP/3 makes QUIC DATAGRAM absence an explicit typed negotiation failure while allowing explicitly negotiated Capsule-only delivery.
A queued DATAGRAM enters the bounded application frame queue immediately and is emitted at the first congestion-, pacing-, recovery-, ACK-, and path-budget opportunity.
A valid DATAGRAM becomes an ordered application event in the same receive transition when finite memory admission succeeds; overload is explicitly droppable and counted.
DATAGRAM application data is legal only at 0-RTT or 1-RTT packet-protection levels.
Applications should be able to prioritize DATAGRAM frames relative to one another and streams.

Adding priorities before expiry, starvation, and scheduler traces are specified would create an unauditable ordering promise; the current deterministic queue is covered while the extension remains explicit residual work.

requirements.summary: A DATAGRAM-only application packet is ack-eliciting but uses the bounded delayed-ACK policy until packet count, reordering, ECN, or max_ack_delay requires an ACK.
DATAGRAM frames enter the common congestion and pacing budget and are delayed in their finite queue or dropped when a changed path can no longer carry them.
The security restatement that every DATAGRAM payload is protected by 0-RTT or 1-RTT keys is enforced at the authenticated packet boundary.

The client never clears the QUIC Bit before processing current peer support.

requirements.summary: HTTP Datagrams are sent only for a request whose extension semantics explicitly authorize them.

A Quarter Stream ID above 2^60-1 is an HTTP/3 connection error of H3_DATAGRAM_ERROR 0x33.
A QUIC DATAGRAM payload too short to decode a Quarter Stream ID is H3_DATAGRAM_ERROR 0x33.

requirements.summary: A client storing HTTP Datagram 0-RTT state must validate the fresh setting against the remembered value.

requirements.summary: Capsule processing failures are surfaced as typed malformed or incomplete message failures.

requirements.summary: A clean stream FIN with a partially retained final Capsule is an incomplete message failure.

Unknown Capsule-Protocol Structured Field parameters do not disable a true Boolean value.

Typed MASQUE requests and successful responses include Capsule-Protocol true for intermediary visibility.

Delay increase is evaluated only after the recommended eight RTT samples in a round.
Conservative Slow Start uses a growth divisor of four, never a value below two.
The paced controller applies all newly acknowledged bytes without the non-paced eight-datagram cap.
HyStart++ runs only for the initial slow start and is disabled after congestion or completed CSS.

standards.title: CUBIC for Fast and Long-Distance Networks

normative_inventory.scope: Atomic uppercase BCP 14 mandatory and advisory clauses; MAY and OPTIONAL are excluded.

requirements.summary: Elapsed CUBIC epoch time excludes intervals where application or flow control prevents window updates.
The Reno-friendly region selects W_est when it exceeds the current CUBIC curve value.
Reno-friendly alpha becomes one once W_est reaches the congestion window saved before reduction.
The concave region increments cwnd by the bounded target-minus-window ratio for acknowledged bytes.
The convex region uses the same bounded per-ACK target-minus-window increment rule.
Packet loss immediately reduces the CUBIC congestion window and slow-start threshold on entering recovery.
Every independent CUBIC congestion response uses the recommended multiplicative factor beta of 0.7.
A cwnd-based implementation prevents congestion-window growth when bytes in flight do not fill cwnd.
The QUIC connection path applies the cwnd-based sparse-flight safeguard before every CUBIC ACK update.
Independent ECN congestion events continue reducing CUBIC until one maximum datagram remains.
Persistent CE at one datagram exponentially reduces pacing rate while retaining one complete send opportunity.
Multi-flow mode shortens W_max with the RFC fast-convergence factor after a lower saturation point.
A known single-CUBIC-flow environment should disable the fast-convergence heuristic.
requirements.reason: The pure controller supports and diagnoses an explicit single-flow mode, but the public runtime has no trustworthy topology signal and currently chooses multi-flow fast convergence by default rather than guessing that an Internet path carries only one flow.

requirements.summary: A TCP retransmission timeout resets W_est to the window at the next congestion-avoidance epoch.
requirements.reason: QUIC has probe timeouts but no TCP retransmission-timeout congestion event; RFC 9438 itself states that QUIC loss is detected only after an acknowledgment, so this TCP-only transition is absent.

requirements.summary: A late optional spurious-loss restoration keeps newer state after cwnd has already exceeded its saved value.
requirements.reason: The optional spurious-fast-retransmit restoration algorithm is not implemented, so there is no saved stale CUBIC state that could overwrite a newer window; ordinary late acknowledgments retain current state.

requirements.summary: CUBIC uses a bounded slow-start algorithm whenever cwnd has not exceeded ssthresh.
The initial CUBIC slow start uses the RFC 9406 HyStart++ delay and Conservative Slow Start states.
The CUBIC curve never uses the inefficient low growth constant C equals 0.04.
The fixed-point curve uses the recommended C equals 0.4 coefficient without floating-point drift.

entries.reason: The rejected proposal would redefine cwnd_prior as flight size; the published definition and RFC 9002 safeguards remain authoritative.

standards.title: Service Binding and Parameter Specification via the DNS (SVCB and HTTPS Resource Records)

requirements.summary: Structured Field parsing is behaviorally equivalent to the RFC algorithms across every mandatory official vector.
The default bounded parser accepts Lists containing at least 1024 members.
The default bounded parser accepts Inner Lists containing at least 256 members.
Order-preserving Parameters have public bounded lookup operations by both wire index and key.
Canonical serialization omits the explicit value for a true Boolean Parameter while retaining false values.
The default parser accepts at least 256 Parameters and Parameter keys of at least 64 characters.
Order-preserving Dictionaries have public bounded lookup operations by both wire index and key.
Unknown Dictionary members remain syntactically accepted and do not prevent independent access to defined members.
Canonical serialization omits the explicit value of a Dictionary member whose Item value is Boolean true.
The default parser accepts at least 1024 Dictionary pairs and keys of at least 64 characters.
A String escape for any character other than DQUOTE or backslash fails the complete parse.
The default parser accepts decoded Strings containing at least 1024 characters.
The default parser accepts Tokens containing at least 512 characters.
The default parser accepts Byte Sequences containing at least 16384 octets after decoding.
Date parsing covers the complete RFC delta-second range spanning all days in years 1 through 9999.
Library-owned fields never choose Display String when String or Token is adequate; the generic codec preserves explicit caller choice only.
Byte Sequence serialization always emits canonical base64 whose unused pad bits are zero.
Matching field lines are combined once in wire order with comma and SP under an aggregate pre-allocation byte limit.
Any syntax or resource failure returns no partial value, selecting the RFC branch that invalidates the complete field value.
A recipient may alternatively reject the complete HTTP message when Structured Field parsing fails.
requirements.reason: The codec selects the RFC's other permitted branch by returning no partial field value; it does not own the enclosing HTTP message or force that optional alternative policy on callers.

requirements.summary: A parser is advised to accept an otherwise valid Byte Sequence whose terminal base64 padding is absent.
requirements.reason: The shared RFC 4648 contract requires padded canonical encodings so digest and signature inputs have one representation; the parser deliberately fails closed instead of synthesizing omitted padding.

requirements.summary: A parser is advised to accept base64 with nonzero unused pad bits when the decoder can be configured accordingly.
requirements.reason: The shared RFC 4648 contract rejects noncanonical pad bits to prevent alternate digest and signature representations of identical bytes; official advisory vectors record this fail-closed choice.

requirements.summary: Byte Sequence parsing rejects characters outside the base64 alphabet and every folded or bare line feed.

normative_inventory.scope: Atomic uppercase BCP 14 mandatory and advisory clauses; MAY and OPTIONAL are excluded.

requirements.summary: A CONNECT request with an empty, absent, non-numeric, or out-of-range target port is rejected before handler admission.
A WebSocket Upgrade client cannot send post-handshake data until a valid 101 response establishes the upgraded connection.
HTTP/1.x CONNECT-UDP datagrams remain unavailable until the 101 Upgrade response is validated.
The proxy client uses the strongest permitted mitigation: it sends only the CONNECT head and waits for a 2xx response before exposing a TCP payload channel.
A rejected HTTP/1.1 CONNECT always closes the underlying connection and discards pipelined bytes regardless of the request or response connection option.

normative_inventory.scope: Atomic uppercase BCP 14 mandatory and advisory clauses; MAY and OPTIONAL are excluded.

requirements.summary: Every RateLimit-Policy list member has a Structured Fields String bare item.
A policy field should remain consistent across a sequence of responses.
requirements.reason: The codec serializes a supplied policy deterministically but deliberately owns no cross-response application policy store, so deployments must enforce semantic consistency at their policy source.

requirements.summary: Every quota policy item carries the required q parameter.
Implementation-specific policy parameters use a vendor-prefixed key.
RateLimit-Policy generation never permits a trailer section.
The q parameter is a non-negative Structured Fields Integer.
The qu parameter is represented only as a Structured Fields String.
A policy w parameter is a positive whole-second Integer.
A policy pk parameter is represented only as a Byte Sequence.
Every service limit item carries the required r parameter.
RateLimit generation never permits a trailer section.
Implementation-specific service-limit parameters use a vendor-prefixed key.
Positive remaining quota is exposed as a pacing hint rather than a service guarantee.
Client advice never assumes full quota restoration after an effective window.
A service-limit pk parameter is represented only as a Byte Sequence.
Retry-After does not end before the advertised effective window.
Generated fields cannot expose quota values above explicit finite application ceilings.
Generated quota-to-window ratios are bounded by an explicit units-per-second ceiling.
A service should document its deployment-specific partition-key generation algorithm.
requirements.reason: This is an application deployment and service-documentation obligation; a generic field codec has no partition algorithm or service documentation to publish.

requirements.summary: Servers should derive partition keys only from information present in the request.
requirements.reason: The codec preserves opaque partition-key bytes and cannot prove their application provenance; request-derived construction remains an explicitly documented server responsibility.

requirements.summary: Each response is interpreted independently without reusing a previous RateLimit field.
Malformed RateLimit fields produce IgnoreRateLimit instead of partial client advice.
Client advice provides bounded minimum request spacing over the effective window.
A valid Retry-After delay takes precedence over every RateLimit hint.
An intermediary replacement cannot make an upstream quota more permissive.
An intermediary should forward a request despite predicting quota rejection.
requirements.reason: The status field codec has no request-forwarding authority; it provides a restrictive mutation guard while the unified proxy policy must make the forwarding decision.

requirements.summary: RateLimit fields on responses with positive current age are ignored.
Available quota is exposed only as bounded advice and never as a service-level agreement.
